html:
Colchis was an ancient kingdom on the Black Sea coast of western Georgia, known to the Greeks as the land of the Golden Fleece, which Jason and the Argonauts sailed to steal.

The myth may reflect real gold: Colchian rivers carried gold dust, and local people are said to have caught it with sheepskins. From the 500s BCE Greek colonies such as Phasis traded on its coast, and the people of the hill city of Vani buried their dead with rich gold jewellery. Colchis was known for linen, timber and wine. It later fell under Pontus and then Rome after Pompey's campaign of 65 BCE. With the eastern Kingdom of Iberia, it is one of the two roots of the Georgian state; see also the polity page Colchis.
